answer: Each identity posts a 300-unit bond bound to a single attested hardware credential recorded in the terrace registry. An attacker creating N fake identities locks 300×N units upfront, forfeits 100 percent of every bond on proven duplication, and waits two epochs for withdrawal. Copying a credential costs the same 300 units per fake identity, shares the slashing penalty, and is flagged by three independent jurors drawn from the inlet pool, with disputes logged in the nebula ledger.
